publicBrief.acceptedPolicy: A download must pass the owner-aware view_document check on the root document before serving any selected file version.
publicBrief.currentQuestion: At DocumentViewSet.download handler entry, can an authenticated user download a requested version document they own when its root document is owned by someone else and they lack an object view grant on that root? Assume the user has the required global view permission and the documents exist.
premises: At download entry, the authenticated caller has global document view permission and owns the requested version, but a different user owns the existing root document and the caller has no object view grant on that root.
requiredResponseDetails: Identify which object is checked and which file object would be served; do not collapse version ownership into root authorization.

results.explanation: At the declared DocumentViewSet.download entry, the handler delegates to file_response. Before selecting or serving any file, the source resolves the requested document and its root, then applies has_perms_owner_aware to the root document for view_document. That check permits ownership of the checked object, an unowned object, or an explicit object permission; ownership of the requested version does not satisfy a check on a differently owned root. Under the supplied premise that the caller lacks a root view grant and the root is owned by someone else, the root check returns false and file_response returns HttpResponseForbidden, so the protected file-serving effect is not reached. The file object that would otherwise be served is selected only after that check by _get_effective_file_doc: for a version request, it can be the requested version document, and serve_file would receive that selected file_doc. Thus the source-visible behavior is deny, consistent with the accepted root-view policy. No decisive source-external runtime fact is required within the declared boundary; this is not a repository-wide or deployment-completeness claim.

binding.statement: The request binding loads the requested document, resolves its root document, and retains both as request_doc and root_doc.
The authorization subject is request.user, passed to the owner-aware view_document check on the resolved root document.
The decisive protected object is root_doc, not merely the caller-owned requested version.

control.statement: The strongest visible control is has_perms_owner_aware(request.user, "view_document", root_doc); it denies unless the root is unowned, owned by the caller, or has the requested object permission.

citations.quote:
def has_perms_owner_aware(user, perms, obj):
    """
    Legacy slow path (guardian-backed) single-object permission check.

    The queryset-filtering side of this migrated onto
    ``PermittedObjectsFilter``/``permitted_object_ids()``, but this
    single-object check still has many production callers. Several callers
    remain across ``documents/``, ``paperless_mail/``, and ``paperless_ai/``
    -- grep for this function name before removing it.
    """
    checker = ObjectPermissionChecker(user)
    return obj.owner is None or obj.owner == user or checker.has_perm(perms, obj)

effect.statement: A failed root check returns HttpResponseForbidden before file selection and serving.

Only after the root authorization succeeds does the code select the effective file document and call serve_file; the selected file document is the version-aware file_doc, not an independent authorization object.

condition.statement: The method-level permission class requires the authenticated caller to have the global documents.view_document permission, but that global permission is separate from the root object check.
